title: Activation matrix, core without module roots, and blocking boundaries
summary: Builds the activation-matrix fixtures and test (knowledge/p3-execution#activation), adds the `core-only` consumer mode that installs the core archive without `modules/` and proves boot/doctor/grant/check, and turns I2, I3, I4, I5 and I13 blocking with empty allowlists.
why: Phase exit: 'core boots, checks and writes without module roots'; release-gate conditions 1–2; architecture#operation-chains I. Hard risks: the inactive-cost assertions must observe real container resolutions and queries (not a mocked container); the core-only archive must really lack module files and providers, otherwise I13 proves nothing.

include: `tests/Fixtures/Activation/**` panels and `tests/Feature/Activation/ActivationMatrixTest.php` covering every row of #activation (core only; Scopes on A not B; Audit on A not B on one storage; two panels with different options and fingerprints; module removed after use with retained rows; DevTools outside console)
`bin/consumer-fixture.sh core-only` mode per #activation, wired as blocking in the consumer CI job (`.github/workflows/*.yml` that runs the consumer fixture)
`tests/Arch/invariants.json`: I2, I3, I4, I5, I13 `blocking: "now"`; report-mode tests assert zero violations; allowlist files emptied/removed per #allowlists with a test that they stay empty
InactiveCost tests extended to the module-roots-present-but-inactive case
exclude: Relocation rehearsal of a separate archive per module (P4)

reads.why: Rules every P3 item follows (reference + amendments win, no shims, placement, oracle, allowlists, snapshots, migration lines, tests)
Exact validation commands, PHP 8.4, driver ports, composer update rule
Which allowlist entries this item removes

rules: Every matrix row has a negative control that fails when the module is activated where it must not be.
